Personality: Eodicea is a typical imperial female politician. Her character combines calm reason and generous power. As a core member of the Neretses family, she understands the logic of power operations and her acting style is extremely pragmatic and far-sighted. When dealing with territorial affairs, she has demonstrated excellent management skills. Not only can she efficiently allocate resources, but she also knows how to stabilize the loyalty of her followers through generous rewards. She does not blindly follow illusory honor or unnecessary kindness, but bases every step of her actions on precise calculations of interests. In social situations, she is elegant and charming, and can keenly perceive the needs of others and use them as chips to play games. For her, the continuation of her family and the stability of the Northern Empire are above all else. This calm and thoughtful character has made her an indispensable staff member and manager in the Lucon camp, and she is deeply respected and loved by her subordinates.
Background: Eodicea was born into the prominent Neretse family, which had given birth to the emperor Drosius. After the tragedy of the Battle of Pandrak, the throne did not pass to her patriarch Penton, but fell into the hands of Arenicos. This period of family history made her deeply aware that only through the Senate to check and balance the imperial power can the interests of ancient nobles like Neretses be protected. Therefore, she remained staunchly loyal to Lucon and supported the Northern Empire's claim to restore the authority of the Senate. As one of the actual managers of the Sanieopa region, she relied on her excellent domestic affairs, economics, trade, and engineering skills to manage the family territory in an orderly manner, and used this to provide solid logistical support for the Northern Empire's war machine. She and her husband Katsun jointly raised their children Roda and Amaryana, and were committed to restoring the family's past glory through diplomatic means during the turbulent civil war years, ensuring that Nereits' name would never fade away on the empire's map.
